claims.text: The initial material is an as-cast or homogenized refractory high-entropy alloy without a pre-formed protective oxide layer.
Pre-oxidation at approximately 1100°C for 1–2 hours at an oxygen partial pressure of 10^-3–10^-5 atm will produce a protective oxide scale on a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The pre-formed oxide scale will be uniform, dense, and adherent.
A CrTaO4-based scale can be protective on a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Chromia and alumina may form part of the protective oxide scale.
The controlled pre-oxidation treatment induces formation of a stable oxide scale.
The stable oxide scale acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion during subsequent high-temperature exposure.
Formation of the stable oxide scale reduces subsequent oxidation.
Formation of the stable oxide scale reduces oxide spallation.
After cyclic oxidation at 1200°C in air for 200 hours, pre-oxidized specimens will have lower mass gain than untreated specimens.
After cyclic oxidation at 1200°C in air for 200 hours, pre-oxidized specimens will have better oxide-scale adhesion and less spallation than untreated specimens.
After cyclic oxidation at 1200°C in air for 200 hours, pre-oxidized specimens will have shallower oxygen penetration than untreated specimens.
Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys directly exposed to the test conditions will undergo greater mass gain, spallation, and oxygen penetration than pre-oxidized alloys.
Poor oxidation resistance is a major obstacle to structural use of refractory high-entropy alloys at high temperature.
The intervention is expected to work only in alloys containing sufficient oxide-forming elements.
Changes in oxygen partial pressure, treatment temperature, or alloy composition may prevent formation of the protective scale.
The optimal oxide composition and microstructure may vary with alloy chemistry and processing conditions.
Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in mass gain and oxygen penetration together with improved scale adhesion would falsify the hypothesis.
